nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.title: Trump's order to split the MMR shot runs into measles outbreaks and a poll showing half of parents believe spacing vaccines out is safer
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.angle: An executive order wants to break the combined MMR shot into three separate vaccines given at different visits. Measles outbreaks in Amish communities are spreading and people are searching for SSPE. The reporting questions: are single-antigen measles, mumps and rubella vaccines even licensed and available in the US, how many more visits would a split schedule take, and what happens to coverage during the gaps? KFF's poll adds a second point: about half of parents wrongly believe spacing vaccines out is healthier, so the order matches a belief people already hold.
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.why_now: The fall 2026 KFF tracking poll came out Oct 20. The executive order is recent, and measles outbreaks plus SSPE searches are exploding this week.
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.is_it_real: KFF is an independent pollster, and the poll numbers belong to KFF. What the order says comes from KFF's summary and has to be checked against the order's text. Whether single-antigen vaccines are available in the US is a question for the reporter to answer, not a fact stated here. The pregnancy COVID-vaccine finding (falling confidence, uncertainty about a false miscarriage claim) is from the same poll series and can be a secondary thread.
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.primary_test: Text of the executive order; FDA's list of licensed vaccines (does a monovalent measles, mumps or rubella product exist in the US?); CDC measles case counts; KFF Tracking Poll topline and methods
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.other_peg: Measles outbreaks in Amish communities in New York and Pennsylvania, and the SSPE search spike Trend Desk flagged

nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.title: $275 million to recruit nursing home nurses: what it buys, and whether Medicaid's state directed payments to nursing homes reach staff at all
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.angle: CMS's Nurses for Nursing Homes program puts $275 million toward roughly 4,000 nurses. KFF's new brief traces how much money states send to nursing homes through state directed payments, and two Boston College CRR papers look at how Medicaid long-term care policy affects aide and nurse jobs and wages. Together they raise a question families care about: when public money goes to nursing homes, does it change staffing at the bedside? Payroll-based staffing data can answer it.
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.why_now: The CMS initiative, the KFF brief and both CRR papers came out Oct 20 to 23, and the federal minimum-staffing rule is still in flux.
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.is_it_real: The $275M figure and the 4,000-nurse estimate are CMS's own and come from a digest summary with no URL, so they need confirming at the CMS newsroom. KFF and CRR are independent analyses; their findings are not in the item text and need reading. The same CMS digest summary also mentions an unrelated ACA eligibility-verification proposed rule (CMS-9873-P), which should not be mixed in.
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.primary_test: CMS Payroll-Based Journal nursing home staffing data; CMS program announcement for Nurses for Nursing Homes; KFF's state directed payment analysis; the CRR working papers

nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.title: Is it real? ESMO week's '75% response' and 'cuts risk 62%' cancer headlines, and the one release that actually shows people living longer
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.angle: In one week, drug companies put out 75%, 77% and 79% response rates (J&J's RIPTAC prostate molecule, Rybrevant in head and neck, Lilly's ovarian ADC) and a '62% lower risk' (Erleada). The test: tumor shrinkage in an early, single-arm trial is not living longer. Only a couple of these releases report overall survival from a Phase III trial (sac-TMT's 25.9 vs 17.4 months; Ziihera's three-year survival). Sort each headline by phase, endpoint and comparator, and show readers how to read the next one.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.why_now: ESMO 2026 releases, Oct 22 to 24. OptiTROP-Lung06 was published in NEJM at the same time.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.is_it_real: Every number is the sponsor's own claim. The response-rate releases appear to be early-phase and single-arm, with no survival data; that has to be confirmed in each registry entry. The release that cuts 'risk by 62%' should be checked for whether the endpoint is recurrence or death or something else, and whether there is overall-survival data. sac-TMT's survival result is a Phase III hard outcome, but the trial population and whether it applies outside China need checking.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.primary_test: ClinicalTrials.gov entries for each trial (phase, arms, primary endpoint); ESMO 2026 abstracts; the NEJM OptiTROP-Lung06 paper

nd-2026-10-27-4-3-million-medicare-enrol.title: 4.3 million Medicare enrollees will lose their Advantage or Part D plan at year's end, and 1.4 million more are in plans being merged: check your mail before Dec 7
nd-2026-10-27-4-3-million-medicare-enrol.angle: A short, useful item for open enrollment: KFF's count from CMS data is 3.1 million Medicare Advantage drug plan enrollees and 1.2 million stand-alone Part D enrollees whose plans end, plus 1.4 million in consolidating plans. It tells readers what a non-renewal notice means and what their options are.
nd-2026-10-27-4-3-million-medicare-enrol.why_now: Open enrollment runs through Dec 7, and terminated plans end Dec 31. Pitching is blocked because this is already widely covered, but the number is usable this week.
nd-2026-10-27-4-3-million-medicare-enrol.is_it_real: These are KFF's analysis of CMS plan data, an independent source. Before running it, confirm the special enrollment period and Medigap guaranteed-issue rights for people whose plans are not renewed against CMS and Medicare.gov guidance. Don't state them from memory.

items.title: More Than 4 Million Medicare Beneficiaries Will Have Their Medicare Advantage or Stand-Alone Prescription Drug Plan Terminated at the End of 2026
items.summary: Data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) shows that 4.3 million Medicare beneficiaries, including 3.1 million Medicare Advantage drug plan enrollees and 1.2 million PDP enrollees, will have their plan terminated at the end of 2026. An additional 1.4 million Medicare Advantage enrollees are in a plan that is consolidating with another plan offered by the same insurer.

nd-2026-10-28-open-enrollment-opens-nov-.title: Open enrollment opens Nov 1 for immigrants who are about to lose coverage they legally hold: the eligibility cutoffs in the 2025 budget law, and the citizen kids dropping off Medicaid out of fear
nd-2026-10-28-open-enrollment-opens-nov-.angle: Not a midterm explainer. The story is the reader clock: refugees, asylees and other lawfully present immigrants who bought marketplace coverage or enrolled in Medicare face eligibility cutoffs around the 2027 plan year. Meanwhile enforcement fear is pushing families to drop coverage for children who are U.S. citizens and still eligible. A secondary angle for her aging lane: nursing homes and home care depend on an immigrant workforce that visa limits now strain.
nd-2026-10-28-open-enrollment-opens-nov-.why_now: ACA open enrollment starts Nov 1 and the midterms are Nov 3. KFF published the update Oct 27. People shopping for 2027 plans now are the ones the eligibility changes hit.
nd-2026-10-28-open-enrollment-opens-nov-.is_it_real: KFF is independent analysis, but the item summary only states in general terms that federal law 'narrowed eligibility' for lawfully present immigrants and that families are avoiding care. It gives no figures here. The specific effective dates I have in mind are from memory and must be confirmed against the statute and CMS guidance before anyone cites them: marketplace premium tax credits limited mainly to green-card holders and a few other groups from 2027, and Medicare eligibility ending for some lawfully present enrollees about 18 months after enactment. The chilling-effect claim needs KFF's own survey data behind it, not just the summary.
nd-2026-10-28-open-enrollment-opens-nov-.primary_test: The text of the 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) eligibility sections, CMS/HHS implementing guidance on marketplace and Medicare eligibility for lawfully present immigrants, and KFF's survey data on immigrant families' coverage and care avoidance
nd-2026-10-28-open-enrollment-opens-nov-.other_peg: ACA open enrollment begins Nov 1, 2026; midterm election Nov 3

items.title: Midterm Election Update: Immigrant Health Policy
items.summary: Immigration restrictions and enforcement are central to the Trump administration’s domestic agenda and a focus of debate in the 2026 midterm elections. These policies have ripple effects on health care: immigration-related fears are leading some immigrant families to avoid medical care and drop coverage, including for U.S. citizen children, and visa restrictions could strain a health care workforce that relies on immigrants. Federal law has also narrowed eligibility for health coverage among lawfully present immigrants, and states are responding in different ways.

nd-2026-10-30-the-0-part-d-plan-is-gone-.title: The $0 Part D plan is gone for 2027: stand-alone drug plan premiums are on track to jump 50%, from $34 to $51 a month, for anyone who doesn't switch by Dec 7
nd-2026-10-30-the-0-part-d-plan-is-gone-.angle: A usable number with a deadline. KFF says no stand-alone Part D plans will have a $0 premium in 2027, so the 4 million-plus people in one now will pay something unless they shop around. The plan with the lowest average premium nationally is Wellcare Value Script at $6.50. AARP Medicare Rx Preferred goes from $126 to $204.50. The deductible cap rises to $700. The take: compare plans before Dec 7, because staying put is what produces the 50% figure. This pairs with Tuesday's roundup item on the 4.3 million people losing their Advantage or Part D plan.
nd-2026-10-30-the-0-part-d-plan-is-gone-.why_now: Open enrollment runs through Dec 7, and KFF published this today (Oct 30). The next Friday roundup still lands with about a month left to switch.
nd-2026-10-30-the-0-part-d-plan-is-gone-.is_it_real: This is KFF's independent analysis of CMS 2027 plan data. The $51 average is a projection that assumes current enrollees stay in their plans and leaves out people getting the Low-Income Subsidy. It's an enrollment-weighted average, not anyone's actual bill. KFF puts the jump down mainly to the loss of $0-premium plans. The release doesn't say whether the scaled-back Part D premium stabilization demonstration played a part, so don't claim a cause beyond what KFF says. I checked the numbers against the KFF page today: $34→$51, 4M+ in zero-premium PDPs, Wellcare $6.50, AARP $204.50, $700 deductible cap, $643 average PDP deductible.
nd-2026-10-30-the-0-part-d-plan-is-gone-.primary_test: CMS 2027 Part D plan landscape files and the CMS 2027 Part D premium and bid announcement

items.title: The Average Monthly Premium for Medicare Part D Stand-Alone Plans Is Projected to Increase by 50% From $34 to $51 in 2027 Unless Enrollees Switch to Lower-Cost Plans
items.summary: A new KFF analysis finds that the average monthly premium for Medicare Part D coverage in stand-alone prescription drug plans (PDPs) will increase to $51 in 2027, up 50% from $34 in 2026, if current enrollees don’t switch into lower-premium plans during open enrollment, which runs through December 7.

items.title: Medicare Part D Premiums and Cost Sharing in 2027
items.summary: Medicare Part D is a voluntary outpatient prescription drug benefit for people with Medicare provided through private plans, including stand-alone prescription drug plans and Medicare Advantage plans that offer drug coverage. This analysis provides an overview of Medicare Part D premiums and cost sharing in 2027 and key trends over time.

nd-2026-10-31-two-months-before-medicaid.title: Two months before Medicaid work requirements start, a federal court has struck down the Trump administration's narrow 'medically frail' exemption in 26 states. Who counts as too sick to work now depends on where you live
nd-2026-10-31-two-months-before-medicaid.angle: The medical frailty exemption decides whether a 58-year-old with COPD, cancer or a mental illness has to log 80 hours a month or lose Medicaid. Massachusetts v. Oz vacated the rule's 'substantially impair' test and barred penalties against the 26 plaintiff states for six months. That leaves a patchwork on Jan. 1: people in the other 17 required states plus DC still face the narrow definition, and under the 2025 law, losing Medicaid over work rules also bars ACA subsidies (KFF).
nd-2026-10-31-two-months-before-medicaid.why_now: The ruling came about Oct. 29, 2026. Work requirements must be in place in 43 states and DC by Jan. 1, 2027, so states are building exemption screens right now, and ACA open enrollment opens Nov. 1.
nd-2026-10-31-two-months-before-medicaid.is_it_real: The ruling comes from Justice in Aging's weekly advocacy newsletter (Oct. 30). That group is an advocate but independent, and it joined an amicus brief in the related case Taylor v. Kennedy. The case name, the 26 states, the vacatur and the six-month penalty bar came from a fetched summary of that newsletter, not from the opinion. Before writing, confirm the court, the date and the scope against the opinion itself. The 43 states plus DC by Jan. 1 and the subsidy bar come from KFF's Oct. 30 open enrollment analysis. Nobody has shown yet how many enrollees the frailty definition affects; that number is the reporting job.
nd-2026-10-31-two-months-before-medicaid.primary_test: The district court opinion and order in Massachusetts v. Oz (PACER / state AG press releases), the CMS rule text defining medical frailty under the 2025 reconciliation law's community engagement requirement, and CBO's coverage-loss estimates for the work requirement
nd-2026-10-31-two-months-before-medicaid.other_peg: Jan. 1, 2027 work-requirement start date; ACA open enrollment opens Nov. 1

nd-2026-10-31-aca-open-enrollment-opens-.title: ACA open enrollment opens Nov. 1: benchmark premiums up 13% for 2027 and 42% since 2025, Cigna is leaving the individual market in all 11 of its states, and there's no longer a cap on paying back subsidies at tax time
nd-2026-10-31-aca-open-enrollment-opens-.angle: KFF's numbers in short: the second straight year of double-digit benchmark increases, people above 400% of poverty paying full price, 11 insurers leaving at least one state, and repayment caps on excess tax credits gone starting with 2026 returns. Use it to tell readers to shop around and re-estimate income before Dec. 15 (the HealthCare.gov deadline; verify), not to auto-renew.
nd-2026-10-31-aca-open-enrollment-opens-.why_now: Open enrollment starts tomorrow, Nov. 1. Readers face higher premiums and fewer insurers this week.
nd-2026-10-31-aca-open-enrollment-opens-.is_it_real: These figures are KFF's own analysis (Oct. 30), drawn from insurer filings, CMS enrollment data and CBO, and should be cited as KFF's. They came from a fetched summary of the page, so recheck them against the page before running. The 2027 open enrollment end date isn't in the item; KFF notes a rule shortening the window was vacated, so confirm the deadline on HealthCare.gov.

items.title: 9 Things to Watch for the 2027 ACA Open Enrollment Period
items.summary: The ACA Marketplace Open Enrollment season begins November 1, bringing higher out-of-pocket premium payments, new eligibility requirements for certain groups, and state efforts to offset premium increases following the expiration of enhanced premium tax credits. Read our analysis of what these and other changes could mean for enrollees.
